correctness.rationale: For hub value zero (one), rim update is AND (OR) of its two cycle neighbors. Two iterations with a constant hub reduce to x_i x_{i-2} x_{i+2} (or its color complement), forcing step-two parity components to be constant, and give two unanimous fixed states plus exactly two fixed-hub two-cycle orbits on even rims. For an alternating hub, the first step is A and the second C; C(A(x))_i=x_i(x_{i-2} OR x_{i+2}). The hub changes 0 to 1 exactly when 2a>n and returns exactly when 2b<n. This yields an if-and-only-if no-isolated-one condition and a bijection to exactly B_n hub-flipping orbits. Cyclic-run compositions give G_l and its odd/even step-two product, with marked-run factor l/r. A symmetric weighted-spin Lyapunov descent with odd local fields excludes longer eventual periods. An injective 110/1100 block construction proves B_n>=2^(n/12) for every n>=96. Python direct graph updates over 262112 configurations n=4..16 and independent word enumeration check the new formulas, but do not replace these finite-to-infinite arguments.

value.rationale: An infinite exact classification and coefficient-formula enumeration of natural deterministic opinion dynamics on centralized wheel networks, plus explicit exponential abundance of reversing-hub attractors, resolves a motivatable dynamical distinction: a hub eliminates all but two fixed points while preserving exponentially many oscillatory behaviors. Published bare-cycle models support the contrast; no downstream theorem is needed because exact recurrent-state structure is the natural object. The finite table verifies rather than motivates the result; neither a tiny parameter increment nor a stand-alone computational count is claimed.
